A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FedNCA-ML work. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across restructuring and renumbering.

before.justification: v3 reports original federated-learning experiments on four datasets, component and query ablations, and feature visualizations, including additional CIFAR-10 analyses in the appendix.

after.justification: v4 retains those experiments and adds original MS COCO comparisons, per-class DermaMNIST ablation results and Grad-CAM examples.

M1.justification: The LADM cross-attention module, shared fixed ETF queries/classifier, BCE and two regularization losses, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. The explanation that ETF anchoring acts on class-wise features clarifies the existing procedure.

E1.justification: v4 adds MS COCO evaluation, extending coverage to an 80-category natural-image benchmark with complex scenes and dense label co-occurrence, compared with the previous maximum of 20 categories. All four earlier datasets remain.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain FedAvg, FedCurv, FedProx, SCAFFOLD, SphereFed, FedLGT and the centralized reference. The added COCO experiment uses this same comparator set; newly discussed related methods are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The new COCO experiment uses beta=0.05 and gamma=0.75, allowing up to 60 of 80 classes per client. v4 also reports individual-class F1 for the DermaMNIST ablation. Existing benchmark settings, the 10-client design, backbone and training budgets are retained.

E4.justification: v4 Table 6 extends the existing DermaMNIST component ablation with per-class F1, exposing which classes benefit. Figure 5 replaces DermaMNIST attention examples with Grad-CAM examples on DermaMNIST and VOC. Existing component/query ablations, t-SNE plots and cosine-similarity analyses remain, including the appendix analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions specify three runs with different random seeds and report means and standard deviations for benchmark comparisons. The new results do not introduce a different uncertainty-reporting practice, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: v4 adds a complete COCO comparison: FedNCA-ML reports macro-AUC 94.10±0.18 and macro-F1 56.28±0.32, with the latter exceeding FedLGT's 55.68±0.83. It also adds seven-class F1 breakdowns and new Grad-CAM findings. All retained benchmark and aggregate ablation scores match; prose corrections include the DermaMNIST ablation F1 gain changing from 7.34 to 7.26 percentage points.

T1.justification: The formal problem, simplex ETF construction, NC properties and mathematical objectives are retained, with no new theoretical results or proofs. Correcting the feature-resolution symbols to H' and W' is a notation repair.

C1.justification: v4 adds an explicit contribution claim that class-wise attention enables NC alignment while preserving semantic relationships in the shared backbone. The central NC-inspired multi-label FL contribution, novelty claim and headline performance gains remain.

C2.justification: v4 acknowledges that a pooled embedding can encode multiple labels, then attributes difficulties under imbalance to entanglement and gradient interference. It adds explanations for preserving backbone semantic relationships and choosing stronger regularization during scratch training. The ChestX-ray14 micro-AUC qualification remains.

D1.justification: Appendix A and Figure 11 document the new COCO partition parameters, class cap and training/test/client label distributions. Existing optimizer, learning rate, training duration and loss-weight disclosures remain unchanged; no new code-access or hardware information is supplied.

R1.justification: Section 2 introduces a local/post/pre-learning taxonomy and explicitly positions FedNCA-ML as pre-learning alignment. It adds discussion supported by works such as FedRS, model-contrastive FL and FedIIC, and clarifies FedMLP's partial-annotation setting. The original claim of first investigating multi-label FL through NC remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work and method explanations undergo extensive rewriting, including a three-challenge narrative and revised contribution list. The separate related-work appendix is removed, dataset documentation moves before supplementary experiments, and missing citation references are repaired.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout. Figure 1 is redesigned, Figure 5 is replaced, the DermaMNIST ablation gains shaded per-class columns, and COCO results/distribution displays and CIFAR-10 sample examples are added. Numerous retained tables and figures are resized or relocated.

improvement.justification: COCO comparisons, per-class ablations and VOC Grad-CAM examples strengthen validation, while clearer explanations and corrected DermaMNIST gain calculations improve accuracy. These benefits are tempered by unnamed per-class columns and imprecise wording: v4 calls 30.27 the lowest per-class F1 although Table 6 also contains 23.83 in that row.
